milestone: Use Case Zero closure — Bankr governed-operation rehearsal: case-bound, exact-spec idempotent draft creation
problem: A migration adding case-bound, exact-spec idempotency to token_launches (services/factor/tokenLaunchService.ts::createOrResumeDraft, called from the Use Case Zero orchestrator's governedOperationRehearsal step) shipped with a unique index PostgREST's generated `ON CONFLICT` clause could never actually resolve at execution time, and simultaneously dropped an existing DB-level invariant (`uq_token_launches_current`, one non-superseded launch per tenant+beneficiary+provider) that the new application logic was not, on its own, a sufficient replacement for. Both defects passed an in-memory fake-Supabase unit test suite cleanly and were only caught on operator review before the migration was applied to live Supabase.
observedFailure: The first version of migration 20260930260000_token_launches_case_bound_idempotency.sql created `uq_token_launches_draft_idempotency` as a PARTIAL unique index: `ON token_launches (tenant_id, draft_idempotency_key) WHERE draft_idempotency_key IS NOT NULL`.

services/factor/tokenLaunchService.ts::createOrResumeDraft called `.upsert(row, { onConflict: 'tenant_id,draft_idempotency_key', ignoreDuplicates: true })` — supabase-js/PostgREST generates a plain column-list `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, draft_idempotency_key) DO NOTHING` for this. Postgres cannot use a PARTIAL index as the arbiter for a column-list `ON CONFLICT` target; the exact reported failure mode is `ERROR: no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification`. This is a live-execution-only failure — no query plan is produced against a fake in-memory table, so tests/use-case-zero-token-launch-idempotency.test.ts's fake Supabase client (which only checked 'does a conflicting row already exist', never asked Postgres to resolve an arbiter index) passed cleanly on the broken migration.

The same first-version migration also `DROP INDEX`-ed `uq_token_launches_current` (tenant_id, beneficiary_agent_runtime_id, provider, WHERE superseded_by IS NULL) outright, removing the one-current-non-superseded-launch-per-beneficiary invariant from the database entirely and leaving `services/factor/tokenLaunchService.ts`'s own application logic as the ONLY thing preventing two concurrent current launches for the same beneficiary — a governance regression independent of, but compounding, the ON CONFLICT defect.

The same first-version application logic also treated a changed rehearsal specification as license to insert an independent, unrelated new row (a different `draft_idempotency_key` computed the same way as a first-time create), rather than treating it as a REVISION of the beneficiary's current launch — contradicting the PRD's immutable-versioning rule (`reviseWithNewVersion`: a changed spec must supersede the prior draft, never fork alongside it).
rootCauses: Belief that `WHERE <col> IS NOT NULL` on a unique index is purely a storage/semantics optimization ("don't bother enforcing uniqueness among rows that don't have the value") rather than also a PLANNER-VISIBLE constraint on which `ON CONFLICT` targets Postgres can resolve. PostgREST/supabase-js's `onConflict` option is translated into a literal column list, and Postgres's `ON CONFLICT (col-list)` inference requires an index whose definition — including any predicate — exactly matches; a partial predicate makes the index structurally ineligible as an inferred arbiter, independent of whether the conflicting row would satisfy that predicate.

The in-memory fake Supabase client built for the unit test suite modeled `.upsert(..., { onConflict, ignoreDuplicates: true })` as "check whether a row already satisfies these columns, and no-op if so" — a faithful model of the DESIRED end-to-end behavior, but not of the INTERMEDIATE mechanism (a real Postgres arbiter-index lookup) that can fail on its own, independent of whether a conflicting row exists. A fake built to the successful-outcome shape rather than to the real transport's own failure modes cannot catch a failure mode that only exists in the real transport.

Treating the (tenant, beneficiary, provider)-scoped one-current-launch invariant and the new (tenant, case, spec)-scoped exact-idempotency invariant as one problem with one index, rather than two genuinely independent invariants that both needed to keep holding simultaneously — leading to reflexively dropping the first index while adding the second, instead of asking whether the first was still needed (it was).
resolution: Migration 20260930260000 corrected: `uq_token_launches_draft_idempotency` is now a FULL, non-partial unique index on (tenant_id, draft_idempotency_key). Postgres already treats every NULL as distinct from every other NULL in an ordinary unique index, so no partial predicate was ever needed to let historical/irrelevant rows carry a NULL key — the partial predicate was solving a non-problem while breaking ON CONFLICT inference. `uq_token_launches_current` is restored verbatim, never dropped.

services/factor/tokenLaunchService.ts::createOrResumeDraft rewritten to read the CURRENT (non-superseded) launch for the beneficiary first (`findCurrentLaunchForBeneficiary`, the exact scope `uq_token_launches_current` enforces); an exact draft_idempotency_key match resumes it with no write; no current launch atomically first-creates via the (now-working) `ON CONFLICT ... DO NOTHING` + read-back; a CHANGED specification calls `reviseWithNewVersion` (extended to accept the same idempotency-key upsert primitive, and to null out the superseded row's own key so a later, genuinely repeated spec can never collide with a defunct row's frozen key) — a revision, never an independent duplicate.

Added `claimDraftForPreflight`: an atomic conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE state = 'draft'` — only the caller whose update actually affects the row proceeds to quote Bankr terms and write the `bankr_launch_preflighted` receipt, so a losing concurrent caller never duplicates either.

Added a REAL PostgreSQL integration test (tests/use-case-zero-token-launch-postgres.integration.test.ts, run via `npm run test:integration` against a live local Postgres 16 instance) that: (a) proves the corrected non-partial index is successfully inferred by the exact PostgREST-generated ON CONFLICT statement; (b) reproduces the ORIGINAL reported defect verbatim as a regression guard, by recreating the old partial index and asserting the exact Postgres error message; (c) races 8 genuinely-concurrent, separate OS-level `psql` processes onto the same insert, proving exactly one row survives; (d) confirms `uq_token_launches_current` still rejects a second concurrent non-superseded row via a plain INSERT, at the database level.

Applied the corrected migration to the live Supabase project and verified, via `pg_indexes`/`information_schema.columns` queries the operator ran directly, that: `uq_token_launches_current` is unchanged (still partial, still scoped to tenant+beneficiary+provider); `uq_token_launches_draft_idempotency` is non-partial (no WHERE clause); `case_ref`/`draft_idempotency_key` exist as `text` columns.
rejectedApproaches: Keeping the partial index and instead having application code pre-check for a conflicting row before every insert (a manual, non-atomic 'select then insert') — rejected: this reintroduces exactly the TOCTOU race the atomic ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING mechanism exists to close; the whole point of pushing the guarantee into Postgres is that it holds even when two OS processes interleave arbitrarily.

Keeping the partial predicate and switching the application code to raw SQL (bypassing PostgREST's `onConflict` inference) so the partial index COULD be targeted directly — rejected: this would work but silently reintroduces a parallel write path outside the Supabase client every other write in this file uses, and the partial predicate was never actually necessary (Postgres's own NULL-uniqueness semantics already provide what it was trying to provide).

Treating the changed-specification case as an independent new row permanently (accepting the governance regression as a deliberate design simplification) — rejected outright: it directly contradicts the PRD's immutable-versioning rule, and would have let multiple simultaneous non-superseded launches accumulate for one beneficiary with no DB-level backstop against it.

incidentRefs: Operator review, 2026-09-07, verbatim: "Five of the six corrections are genuinely present, but the new Bankr database idempotency mechanism has a PostgreSQL-level defect that the fake-Supabase test cannot catch... Supabase/PostgREST generates column-based ON CONFLICT. PostgreSQL cannot infer that partial unique index without the matching predicate, so live execution is liable to fail with: no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification."

Operator's own live-Supabase verification queries and results confirming the corrected schema (uq_token_launches_current preserved partial/tenant+beneficiary+provider-scoped; uq_token_launches_draft_idempotency non-partial; case_ref/draft_idempotency_key present as text) after this resolution's migration was applied.
